New season? Same uniform 👏🏻 👏🏻 👏🏻 

There is so much over consumerism in the U.S. promoting sports teams to require kids to have new uniforms or kits each season, typically costing parents multiple hundreds of dollars per year. 

In Spain, our federated league in Madrid changes uniforms/kits every two to four seasons!!!!, letting parents invest in a kit once that will last several years. 

Sponsors don’t change every year, so kits don’t either. 

Parents pay a seasons fee on our team (480€ or $530 for the season) but no additional uniform costs - only for the new families or when sizing replacements are needed. 

The kit is part of the club’s identity, not just more merchandise to fill a landfill one day. 

In the U.S. 🇺🇸, clubs may rely on uniform revenue. Many clubs intentionally design new uniforms every year so that the players have to buy the new uniform. 

Another way life in  Spain feels simple to our all-American 🇺🇸 family👏🏻

Our American 🇺🇸 family has now lived in three areas in the comunidad of Madrid, and hands down the best to go to school and live in is:

TRES CANTOS 🇪🇸 (specifically, Nuevo Tres Cantos if you prefer new construction!)

Tons of options of good public, concertado and international/American schools, its own city with a 20 min-direct Renfe ride into centro Madrid, urbas full of families outside day and night, walkable and safe at all hours, fútbol pitches, full kid independence, great fútbol teams, an international makeup but mostly local Spanish families. 

I’ll save your time if you’re looking for the best place to raise a family in the community of Madrid - it’s here.

Here’s how it works:

Because we departed from Spain (or any EU country), EU Regulation 261/2004 (EU261) is in play, which is one of the strongest passenger‑rights laws in the world.

- over 3 hour delay
- international flight (Madrid to Philadelphia)

We qualify for compensation! 600€ per passenger. 

We also qualified for 20€ per person on credits for food and beverage in the airport and if we were delayed longer even more. 

But they aren’t going to hand it to you: YOU need to initiate. 

You simply look on the airline’s website for a EU261 form OR send them an email with your information (boarding passes, proof of delay on your app showing new time, passenger names and seat numbers). They are legally required to pay you this no matter where you are from because you left from a Spanish airport: a flat 600€ per passenger regardless of flight destination 😮 (this is for long haul flights only)

There are a few exceptions like strikes and weather, but today poor crew planning and a change of aircraft qualified us for a 2400€ payout 💰

Everyone is trying to come up with a genius way to move to Spain: build a business, find some form of past family heritage, marry a Spaniard (no, I didn’t 😉 ) 🤣

But the solution may be all around you. 

You have kids to enroll in a school. 
Schools have a need for American English speaking volunteers or staff - especially American schools - throughout Spain. 

You’re a doctor? You could be the school nurse. 
You run an IT firm? You could teach an IT class. 

This year, I’ll actually be teaching an elective on Intro to Social Media to secondary students at our school in Madrid. 

You don’t need to have any background or even interest in education. 

Many American schools abroad provide not just a housing stipend (we received 900€/month for the first year which isn’t too shabby!), but also reduced tuition for your children and/or coverage of a visa. 

My number one tip people don’t consider: contact American schools in the country you’re considering a move to - send your resume (even without a teaching background) and see how you could become volunteer or paid staff. 

A lot of times this can be your ticket abroad for several years right here. It worked for us!

(That could mean over $8000/year in just Spanish social security, not taxes) to live/work in Spain. 😮 

If you fall in what they call the “middle income tramos”, that’s still 320€ per month from 80€, or $4500/year. 

And this isn’t just for self-employed “millionaires”: this would be for autónomos year two who make around $70,000. 

The most important discussion you need to have with your lawyer BEFORE moving to Spain: what will be your YEAR TWO tax AND social security estimates be. 

One of the most important decisions you’ll make is an immigration lawyer that understands Spanish tax and social security, too, and can help estimate these potential year two and on costs for you up front. results.caption:
In my 41 years, we’ve never had a trip go as crazy as our August trip to Mallorca did. 

We have visited Mallorca in November 2023 and had a wonderful trip and always wanted to go back in summer to experience the warm, clear waters. 

Apparently everyone else in Europe did, too. 

- three hour rental car waiting lines
- packed restaurants 
- packed beaches 
- airport delays 
- although I had secured low airline flights, rentals were 3x what we paid in November 2023

It didn’t feel like responsible tourism, it felt more like overtourism. 

We learned that September - June are the perfect times to travel around Spain (with the exception of northern Spain - that always seems to be like a good time!) and the southern coastline (Costa del Sol) and islands, to avoid in July and August.  I do though think Cadiz is always a good idea 😉
